## Setup

library(readr)

## Load Data

```{r}
# AI prompt: Use a repository-root-relative path to import the NHANES CSV.
# Verified: The path resolves and the CSV imports when rendered from the repository root.
nhanes <- read_csv("examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
```

## Inspect

```{r}
cat("Rows:", nrow(nhanes), "\nColumns:", ncol(nhanes), "\n")
names(nhanes)

variable_inspection <- data.frame(
  variable = names(nhanes),
  type = vapply(nhanes, function(column) class(column)[1], character(1)),
  missing = colSums(is.na(nhanes))
)
variable_inspection
```

## Summarize

Compare body mass index (BMI) across income groups, using records with non-missing BMI and income group.

```{r}
# AI prompt: Prepare BMI and income-group records for grouped BMI summaries, and write a reusable mean/SD function.
# Verified: BMI and IncomeGroup exist in the imported data; the pipeline excludes missing values, and the rendered summaries run.
nhanes_analysis <- nhanes |>
  filter(!is.na(BMI), !is.na(IncomeGroup)) |>
  mutate(IncomeGroup = trimws(IncomeGroup)) |>
  select(IncomeGroup, BMI, Age, Gender)

bmi_summary <- nhanes_analysis |>
  group_by(IncomeGroup) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_bmi = mean(BMI),
    sd_bmi = sd(BMI),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

bmi_summary
```

## Function

```{r}
# AI prompt: Return the non-missing count, mean, and SD for a numeric vector.
# Verified: The helper runs on analysis-ready BMI values and returns n, mean, and sd.
mean_sd <- function(x) {
  values <- x[!is.na(x)]
  data.frame(
    n = length(values),
    mean = mean(values),
    sd = sd(values)
  )
}

mean_sd(nhanes_analysis$BMI)
```

## Save Output

```{r}
dir.create("assignments/assignment02-r-with-ai/submission/output", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
write_csv(bmi_summary, "assignments/assignment02-r-with-ai/submission/output/summary_table.csv")
```
